prompt: State the principle of conservation of energy, and explain why a ball dropped onto a hard floor does not bounce back to its original height.
markscheme:
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or transformed; the total energy of an isolated system is constant **(A1)**

On impact some kinetic energy is transferred to internal energy (heating) and sound, so less is available to convert back to gravitational potential energy **(R1)**

prompt: A 20 kg box is lifted vertically through 1.5 m at constant speed. How much work is done by the lifting force? ($g=9.8\ \text{m s}^{-2}$)
markscheme: **B.** At constant speed the lifting force equals the weight, 196 N; $W=Fs=196\times1.5=294$ J $\approx290$ J, transferred to gravitational potential energy.

prompt:
A lamp takes in 60 W of electrical power and emits 12 W as visible light; the rest is thermal energy.

**(a)** Calculate its efficiency. **[1]**

**(b)** Describe the Sankey diagram for the lamp. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\dfrac{12}{60}=0.20$ (20%) **(A1)**

**(b)** An input arrow of width representing 60 W splits into a useful light arrow one-fifth of the width (12 W) continuing forward **(A1)**, and a wasted thermal arrow four-fifths of the width (48 W) bending away **(A1)**. Widths are proportional to power.

prompt:
A sled is pulled 30 m along level ground by a rope with tension 80 N at $25^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.

**(a)** Calculate the work done by the tension. **[2]**

**(b)** State the work done on the sled by the normal force, with a reason. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $W=Fs\cos\theta=80\times30\times\cos25^{\circ}$ **(M1)** $=2.2\times10^{3}$ J **(A1)**

**(b)** Zero: the normal force is perpendicular to the displacement ($\cos90^{\circ}=0$) **(R1)**

prompt: A 1200 kg car accelerates from $10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ to $20\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ over 150 m on level ground. Calculate the average resultant force on the car.
markscheme:
Work by resultant force = change in kinetic energy: $\Delta E_k=\tfrac12(1200)(20^{2}-10^{2})=1.8\times10^{5}$ J **(M1)(A1)**

$F=\dfrac{1.8\times10^{5}}{150}=1.2\times10^{3}$ N **(A1)**

prompt: A child on a trampoline is momentarily at rest at the lowest point, with the trampoline fully stretched. Their mechanical energy at this instant is stored mainly as:
markscheme: **C.** At rest, $E_k=0$; at the lowest point the gravitational potential energy is at its minimum, and the stretched trampoline stores elastic potential energy. Mechanical energy = $E_k+E_p+E_H$.

prompt:
A roller-coaster car starts from rest at a height of 20 m and runs down a frictionless track. Take $g=9.8\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.

**(a)** Calculate its speed at a height of 8.0 m. **[2]**

**(b)** Explain why the answer does not depend on the shape of the track or the mass of the car. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $mg\Delta h=\tfrac12mv^{2}\Rightarrow v=\sqrt{2\times9.8\times12}$ **(M1)** $=15\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ **(A1)**

**(b)** With no resistive forces, mechanical energy is conserved; only the change in height matters, and $m$ cancels from both sides **(R1)**

prompt: A spring with $k=400\ \text{N m}^{-1}$ is compressed by 0.10 m and used to launch a 0.050 kg ball vertically upwards. Ignoring air resistance and the spring's mass, calculate the height the ball rises above its launch point. Take $g=9.8\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.
A truck and a bicycle have the same momentum. The truck's mass is 100 times the bicycle's. What is $\dfrac{E_k(\text{bicycle})}{E_k(\text{truck})}$?
markscheme: **D.** $E_k=\dfrac{p^{2}}{2m}$: with equal $p$, kinetic energy is inversely proportional to mass, so the bicycle has 100 times the kinetic energy.

prompt:
**(a)** A motor lifts a 50 kg load at a constant $0.80\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the useful power output. **[2]**

**(b)** A car travels at a constant $30\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ against total resistive forces of 800 N. Calculate the power developed by the engine. **[2]**

Take $g=9.8\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.
markscheme:
**(a)** $F=mg=490$ N at constant speed; $P=Fv=490\times0.80$ **(M1)** $=390$ W **(A1)**

**(b)** Constant velocity, so driving force $=800$ N **(M1)**; $P=800\times30=2.4\times10^{4}$ W **(A1)**

prompt: An electric motor takes 500 W of electrical power and lifts a 50 kg mass through 6.0 m in 8.0 s at constant speed. Calculate the efficiency of the motor. Take $g=9.8\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.

A car needs 180 MJ of stored energy for a journey. Petrol stores about 46 MJ per kilogram; a lithium-ion battery stores about 0.90 MJ per kilogram.

**(a)** Calculate the mass of each needed to store 180 MJ. **[2]**

**(b)** Suggest why electric cars are nonetheless competitive. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Petrol: $\dfrac{180}{46}=3.9$ kg; battery: $\dfrac{180}{0.90}=200$ kg **(A1)(A1)**

**(b)** Electric motors are far more efficient (about 90% vs about 25–30% for a petrol engine), so less stored energy is needed for the same journey; energy can also be recovered in braking **(R1)**

(Energy per unit mass is often called specific energy; energy per unit volume is energy density. Both matter for vehicles.)
